findings.observedWork: A new Worker with job data is made per job; ONNX adapters create InferenceSession and release it in finally (e.g.enhancement worker 185/236, Kokoro109/140).
findings.proposedChange: Retain a bounded model session in an isolated reusable worker keyed by authenticated artifact digest and exact settings, retiring the worker on failure/cancel and unloading after idle policy.
findings.scenario: Generate successive Kokoro speech lines or enhance multiple selections using the same installed model.
findings.validation: Second/third job inference-start latency, total warm Generate latency, model-load CPU, RSS cap and cancellation/foreign-job isolation tests.
findings.existingProtection: Family utility processes already stay warm 120s; that avoids family handshake only, not current per-job inner worker/model-session load.
findings.correctness: Needs worker protocol/lifetime redesign, exact artifact invalidation and bounded RSS; per-job termination currently guarantees cleanup.

findings.title: Avoid restarting Whisper and loading its model per VAD segment
findings.observedWork: Each detected voice-activity segment is written to segment.wav and then runWhisperCli spawns the CLI with --model (229-250).
findings.proposedChange: Use a supervised batch/native Whisper session that retains one authenticated model for all VAD ranges, preserving per-range timestamps and deterministic language settings.
findings.scenario: Transcribe a 30-minute interview with many short pauses/VAD ranges.
findings.validation: CLI spawn count, model load time, transcript wall time, real-time factor and segment offset/language/tokens parity.
findings.existingProtection: VAD already skips silence and segment staging is bounded; model reuse targets the repeated cost introduced by segmented invocation.
findings.correctness: Likely requires new runtime binding/engine closure and manual Update AI assets if implemented through a native library/batch wrapper.

findings.title: Reuse a supervised llama model and invariant prompt prefix
findings.observedWork: Every editorial job runs llama CLI with --model and --single-turn; utility family warmth does not preserve the CLI model/KV state.
findings.proposedChange: Introduce a supervised offline inference service with digest-bound resident model and reusable invariant prompt prefix; reset job-specific state and retire on cancel/failure.
findings.scenario: Generate successive editorial proposals against the same transcript/context with a local Qwen model.
findings.validation: Repeated Generate latency, model reloads, tokens/sec, prefix evaluation time, deterministic JSON/grammar outputs and cross-job data isolation.
findings.existingProtection: CLI already disables network/device offload and bounds tokens/output; maintain those exact authenticated policies.
findings.correctness: Architectural runtime/protocol change; runtime bytes/closure changes would require manual Update AI assets. A persisted prompt cache must never leak another project.

findings.title: Tune inference thread budgets to actual desktop hardware and competing work
findings.observedWork: ONNX fixes intraOp threads to 4 and interOp to 1; Whisper/llama also hardcode4, while Sherpa defaults2.
findings.proposedChange: Derive a bounded shared inference thread budget from available cores and active work, benchmark task-specific choices, and preserve UI/audio headroom under concurrent jobs.
findings.scenario: Generate while editing on a two-core laptop versus a 16-core desktop.
findings.validation: Generate p50/p95, inference throughput, dropped playback packets, timeline frame times and CPU contention at 2/4/8 thread settings.
findings.existingProtection: Native family processes already run at background scheduling priority and power etiquette applies; threads remain a separate budget.
findings.correctness: More threads can slow inference and harm responsiveness; use measured task-specific thresholds rather than always maximizing cores.
findings.evidenceLevel: hardware tuning experiment; benefit must be established separately for each task and core count

findings.title: Avoid recomputing DeepFilter overlapping context features
findings.observedWork: Default 4-second cores include 1-second context on each side; source frames and full analysis are reread/recomputed for adjacent windows.
findings.proposedChange: Cache overlap PCM/STFT/ERB feature work where normalization semantics allow, or increase the bounded core span under Speed after boundary quality tests.
findings.scenario: Enhance a 20-minute multichannel recording.
findings.validation: Analyzed frames/source frame, prep DSP CPU, total enhancement real-time factor and seam/reference error.
findings.existingProtection: Current bounded windowing intentionally uses overlap for context and avoids whole-recording memory; keep context semantics.
findings.correctness: Feature normalization/state differs by window; cannot reuse normalized features blindly or discard context for speed.

findings.title: Batch or pipeline independent DeepFilter channel work
findings.observedWork: For each chunk, channels are analyzed, inferred and synthesized sequentially, with a model batch dimension fixed to 1.
findings.proposedChange: Pipeline bounded channel analysis/synthesis against the existing inference session, reserving UI cores. Only consider model batching after a separately authenticated model graph demonstrates compatible batch geometry; current model fixes batch dimension to one.
findings.scenario: Enhance an eight-channel dialogue recording using the same network.
findings.validation: Channel batch throughput, whole enhancement time, RSS and per-channel reference/boundary equality.
findings.existingProtection: One ONNX session currently uses 4 CPU threads; naive parallel sessions may oversubscribe rather than improve speed.
findings.correctness: Batch support must be established from model graph, not assumed; preserve channel independence and 4-second output order.

findings.title: Reuse DeepFilter Bluestein transform scratch buffers
findings.observedWork: Every transformBluestein forward call allocates two Float64Array buffers of convolutionSize; analysis/synthesis call this for many960-sample FFT frames.
findings.proposedChange: Create a job-owned/reentrant transform workspace and reuse workReal/workImaginary with required tail zeroing, or evaluate a tested960-point native/SIMD FFT adapter.
findings.scenario: Enhance a long recording, where hundreds of FFT frames occur in every source window.
findings.validation: Allocations/FFT frame, DSP CPU, worker GC pause, full Generate latency and deterministic/reference tolerance tests.
findings.existingProtection: FFT_PLAN, sine/cosine and convolution kernel are already precomputed; this candidate specifically targets repeated scratch allocation.
findings.correctness: Never share mutable scratch across concurrent channel transforms; a native engine replacement could require runtime-asset update.

findings.title: Stream Kokoro output chunks into its reserved WAV sink
findings.observedWork: All generated Float32 waveforms are retained in chunks, then encodePcm16Wave constructs full output before publishAssistanceOnnxOutput writes it.
findings.proposedChange: Write quantized PCM chunks into the authenticated reserved sink as each sentence finishes, maintain incremental digest/frame count and finalize the WAV header atomically.
findings.scenario: Generate a multi-paragraph narration approaching the 128 MiB output reservation.
findings.validation: Peak worker RSS, post-inference encode/publication latency, total Generate time and exact WAV/header/sample/digest parity.
findings.existingProtection: Output reservation and token chunks are bounded, but all successful chunks remain resident until final encode.
findings.correctness: Cancellation must rollback incomplete WAV; do not mark output authenticated or playable before final sealed digest/geometry.

findings.title: Reuse an authenticated G2P closure within a supervised speech worker lifetime
findings.observedWork: Every phonemize request loads manifest, inventories every closure file and hashes them serially before spawning the helper; authenticateClosure loop is175-178.
findings.proposedChange: Authenticate a private immutable closure/snapshot once for a bounded supervised worker lifetime, pin exact identity and invalidate/reverify on changes; optionally keep the G2P subprocess warm.
findings.scenario: Generate many short speech lines where inference itself is short.
findings.validation: Generate-to-first-token latency, closure bytes hashed/request, G2P process starts and tamper/replacement invalidation tests.
findings.existingProtection: Exact target inventory and no-follow file authentication are intentional; retain them. Current per-job ONNX worker limits practical cache reuse until its lifecycle changes.
findings.correctness: Never replace digest verification with mtime-only trust. A persistent helper or different archive closure may require manual AI-asset update.

findings.title: Detach only changed immutable project branches for publication
findings.observedWork: The existing top-level WeakMap reuses a detached project while its identity stays unchanged. Every new canonical project identity recursively copies/freezes the entire project with a new traversal WeakMap, including unchanged clips, tracks and metadata. Soundscaper's clone helper currently structuredClone-copies the document, so a nested-identity cache alone cannot reuse those newly cloned leaves.
findings.proposedChange: Introduce explicit immutable ownership and copy-on-write authored updates, then retain detached unchanged subtrees by owned identity/version; publish only edited paths. An alternative is a trusted command change-set for incrementally updating the detached view. Keep full detachment for untrusted/mutable inputs.
findings.scenario: Change one clip, track property or time selection in a 10,000-100,000-clip Soundscaper project.
findings.validation: Visited/copied snapshot nodes and allocated bytes per small edit, snapshot build CPU, command-to-visible-result p50/p95, retained cache bytes.
findings.existingProtection: PUBLISHED_PROJECTS already avoids copying on status-only publications with the same project identity; VIDEO_PREVIEW_PROJECTS, project lists and preferences have their own identity caches. Preserve proxy detachment, cyclic identity, read-only Map/Set behavior and capability branding. This requires immutable update ownership, not a blind global WeakMap.
findings.measurement: Operation probe: 10,000 clip leaf reads on first publication, zero with unchanged project identity, 10,000 again for root-only selection replacement retaining the same clips. Production updates currently clone the full document; copy-on-write prerequisite remains.

findings.title: Retain effect-type catalog snapshots for each registry and locale
findings.observedWork: Every document publication remaps the rack and selection effect registries into fresh frozen objects, recomputes hasSettings using Object.keys, and obtains a fresh video-definition array even when the registry/copy has not changed.
findings.proposedChange: Build the frozen effect catalogs once per snapshot composition or cache them by registry revision and localized copy identity; preserve invalidation when translations or registry contents change.
findings.scenario: Rapid controller status updates, Apply completion or macro steps while an effect menu/inspector is mounted.
findings.validation: Registry mapping/Object.keys invocations and effect-catalog allocations per publication; snapshot build CPU and dependent menu renders.
findings.existingProtection: The source effect definitions already have stable module ownership; this targets their repeatedly derived UI catalogs. Locale must remain part of the cache identity.

findings.title: Reuse admitted preset normalization and per-effect lists
findings.observedWork: Every document snapshot calls listAudioEditorEffectPresets, which normalizes every saved preset, checks ID uniqueness and freezes another normalized state before filtering for the current effect and appending factory presets. Unrelated project/status publications repeat this work over the whole library.
findings.proposedChange: Retain normalization at an explicit admission boundary for an immutable preset-state identity, and cache its display list by preset revision/current effect/factory registry revision. Keep validation for arbitrary imported or mutable inputs.
findings.scenario: Use a large imported user-preset library, then apply several effects or update selections without changing that library.
findings.validation: Preset normalizations and allocated parameter objects per publish, snapshot build CPU at 100/1,000/5,000 saved presets, preset-menu render counts.
findings.existingProtection: Preset CRUD returns frozen normalized states. This must not bypass import/type/timestamp/duplicate-ID validation or assume arbitrary caller objects are immutable.
findings.measurement: Operation probe: two unchanged listings each copy all 1,000 already-normalized user presets into new objects.

findings.title: Retain detached macro and script libraries until their revision changes
findings.observedWork: Every snapshot recursively materializes and freezes the entire macro library and script library using a fresh traversal map, although their services replace library state only on explicit library edits/imports. Unlike preferences and project lists, these potentially large detached values have no retained publication identity.
findings.proposedChange: Cache detached macros/scripts by the controller-owned immutable library identity or explicit revision; return a stable frozen empty value. Invalidate on import/save/delete and preserve mutation isolation.
findings.scenario: A session with hundreds of macros or large scripts while other commands repeatedly publish status or project snapshots.
findings.validation: Library entries/script bytes copied and allocated per unrelated publish, snapshot CPU, dependent macro menu render count, bounded retained memory.
findings.existingProtection: Macro execution ownership/cancellation is separate; this only reuses UI-facing library snapshots. Existing materialization preserves cycles and read-only collections and must continue to do so.

findings.title: Batch synchronous controller presentation transitions into one publication
findings.observedWork: setStatus and showAnalysis publish immediately. Analysis begin first sets busy, then setLocalizedStatus triggers a snapshot, then explicitly publishes an identical state again. Success publishes result, status and finally busy=false separately. SnapshotChannel rebuilds synchronously and notifies listeners on every call even when React can batch later rendering.
findings.proposedChange: Add explicit scoped presentation transactions or no-publish state setters so each synchronous busy/start and completion transition publishes once after all owned fields are set. Suppress identical status replacements. Preserve an initial busy publication before expensive work begins.
findings.scenario: Analyze a short selection, repeat a cached analysis, or finish several macro/effect steps that update result/status/busy together.
findings.validation: Snapshot builds/subscriber notifications per operation and build CPU; busy-first-paint and final-result latency; cancellation/stale-owner tests.
findings.existingProtection: Realtime telemetry already has a separate channel. Do not defer busy state across the compute phase or allow an older task's finish to clear a newer task's busy flag.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed duplicate synchronous build path; React frame impact unmeasured

findings.title: Publish the requested specialized analysis before independent generic metrics finish
findings.observedWork: Plot Spectrum and Find Clipping await renderAndAnalyze, including complete EBU/true-peak/generic metrics, before starting their independent report computation. The specialized report cannot become visible until both serial phases finish.
findings.proposedChange: After the single authored mix render, start specialized reporting and generic metrics as independent owned tasks; publish the specialized report as soon as ready, then publish the completed generic metrics/visuals. Retain all existing metrics and disable/export or mark incomplete payloads until they are complete.
findings.scenario: Plot spectrum or find clipping on a long selection where generic loudness and true-peak processing dominate the requested report's first-result latency.
findings.validation: Click-to-specialized-report first paint versus click-to-complete-analysis, total CPU, extra buffer bytes and renderer frame gaps; report equality and project-change cancellation.
findings.existingProtection: Generic analysis already executes in a worker. AnalysisPanel currently shows generic metrics in every mode and exports result+report, so eliminating that work would change behavior. This is scheduling/progressive publication, not deletion of required metrics. Contrast needs RMS first and should only use this after preserving exact generic RMS semantics.
findings.correctness: Bind partial and complete metrics/report/visuals to the same request and revision; clear or mark previous generic metrics while partial results are displayed. Preserve the complete export contract.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed serial dependency; first-result benefit unmeasured

findings.title: Persist completed analysis after displaying the result
findings.observedWork: On a levels-analysis cache miss, the complete result and visuals are ready but the service awaits cache persistence before showAnalysis. Slow analysis-store writes delay result visibility; a cache write failure prevents the computed report from being shown.
findings.proposedChange: Assert ownership and publish the complete result first, then schedule bounded tracked cache persistence outside the display critical path with captured revision/key and explicit failure handling. Preserve flush/disposal semantics where required.
findings.scenario: Analyze a selection while the project's storage backend is busy writing PCM or autosave data.
findings.validation: Time from DSP completion to analysis first paint, injected cache-write latency versus UI completion, persistence queue depth and retry/error behavior.
findings.existingProtection: A revision/scope/range levels cache already exists. This preserves its contents and admission checks while removing successful cache persistence from the visible-result dependency.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed critical-path await; storage-delay impact depends on backend

findings.title: Run spectrum, clipping and delivery loudness reporting off the renderer
findings.observedWork: After rendering, specialized spectrum averages every half-overlapping FFT window synchronously; clipping scans every sample synchronously; Measure Loudness calls synchronous EBU measurement. These direct calls run in the renderer despite generic levels analysis already having a worker implementation.
findings.proposedChange: Extend a bounded analysis worker protocol with specialized report jobs, ordered chunking/backpressure and cancellation; keep numerical reporting algorithms unchanged. Borrow/copy/transfer PCM according to explicit ownership, since the same channels may feed generic metrics and visuals.
findings.scenario: Plot spectrum with a large FFT on a multi-minute mix, Find Clipping on many channels, or Measure Loudness while the timeline is playing.
findings.validation: Renderer long-task maximum and p95 animation frame interval during each analyzer, click-to-report latency, worker CPU and peak memory; exact bins/regions/loudness equivalence.
findings.existingProtection: analyzeChannelsInWorker already offloads generic peak/RMS/EBU work and copies bounded chunks. Do not claim generic analysis lacks a worker, and do not detach buffers still needed by another analysis/visual consumer.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed synchronous sample/FFT loops; Electron trace needed

findings.title: Cache specialized reports by authored content and normalized analysis options
findings.observedWork: The levels path uses a project/revision/scope/track/range cache, while spectrum, clipping and loudness commands always rerender and recompute. Repeating an unchanged specialized request pays the full offline rendering, generic analysis and report cost again.
findings.proposedChange: Use a bounded revision-keyed complete-report cache for spectrum/clipping/loudness, including normalized effective FFT size, threshold/consecutive count, selected scope, ADM weighting and relevant render/runtime settings. Reuse the generic results/visuals where keys match. Validate admission before lookup and invalidate on any audible-content/settings change.
findings.scenario: Repeat Analysis or manually run the same spectrum/clipping report repeatedly on an unchanged selection, or measure unchanged delivery loudness twice.
findings.validation: Offline renders and sample/FFT passes per identical repeat, repeat click-to-report p50/p95, cache hit rate/bytes and invalidation correctness.
findings.existingProtection: Levels caching is already implemented, and the inspector deduplicates automatic requests for the same content key while mounted. This addresses explicit repeats and mode/report reuse; it does not claim automatic duplicates occur on every render.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed absent specialized cache; benefit workload-dependent

findings.title: Retain command projections within the admitted immutable controller document
findings.observedWork: Each controller command read calls the product command projection again. Soundscaper validates the complete canonical document, then resolves and freezes all timeline clips, tracks, project-bin clips and annotations. Runtime projection branding only avoids resolving an already projected result; the controller reader does not retain that result for its unchanged canonical identity.
findings.proposedChange: Memoize the product command/runtime projection in the controller reader for the admitted immutable project identity (plus any projection-relevant runtime policy), invalidating on document replacement. Retain uncached validation for arbitrary mutable external inputs and preserve product-owned extension fields.
findings.scenario: Several command consumers/enablement queries or repeated edit setup against the same large current document before its next mutation.
findings.validation: Canonical validation/projection invocations and projected clip allocations per current identity, controller preparation CPU and command-to-result latency on 10,000-100,000 clips.
findings.existingProtection: The resolver already shares one coordinate context within a projection and branded runtime projections pass through unchanged. This adds cross-query reuse under controller ownership; a global identity cache for arbitrary mutable projects would be incorrect.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed repeated projection entry point; representative query frequency/impact unmeasured
